column3: ἀληθής means true or truthful, rendered as “valid.”
ἀληθής means true or truthful, rendered as “valid.”
The Greek contrasts the clauses with “but”; BSB recasts the opening as concessive “Even though.”
“John” makes the Greek pronoun explicit; “bask” renders the Greek “rejoice.”
The Greek says “greater” rather than specifying “more substantial.”
The Greek says “in them” and identifies the Scriptures themselves as testifying; BSB says “by them” and “these very words.”
“Yet” makes a contrast explicit where the Greek has “and.”
The Greek says “you do not receive Me” in the present, rather than “have not received.”
The Greek makes the opening conditional, “if,” rather than causal “since.”
